model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Q2-2026 earnings release (8-K ex99.1, 2026-07-29): H1-26 SBC $24.7M legacy (FY2025 $39.9M per 10-K cash-flow add-back); equity-award withholding taxes FY2025 $8.6M. Pro forma SBC ~$58M/yr incl. ~$8M NSA platform; +~$8M award taxes = $66M (1.17% of pro forma revenue). Core FFO is already AFTER the SBC expense; the engine adds it back into the EBITDA line and charges it explicitly via sbc_pct_path so the house/street band is visible. FAD (company) adds back 'SBC in excess of cash paid' -- the house basis does not.
inputs.fy0: FY2026 (pro forma run-rate incl. NSA and PS Canada)
inputs.share_count_basis: Pro forma fully diluted common shares + OP units = 195.0M: 176.51M Q2-26 weighted diluted (10-Q cover 175.62M common at 2026-07-21, pre-close) + 10.81M PSA common issued to NSA shareholders (77.21M NSA common at 2026-05-01 x 0.1400) + 4.10M PSA OP units to former NSA OP unitholders (8-K 2026-07-22 item 3.02) + 2.76M PSA OP units to PS Canada sellers (8-K 2026-09-01) + 0.80M ATM forward-sale shares (796,009 at $326.32, ~$258M proceeds, unsettled at Q2; proceeds fund acquisitions whose NOI is in the run-rate). OP units are economically identical to common (exchangeable 1:1). EXCLUDED: PS Canada earn-out of up to $288M in OP units at $375/unit (~0.77M units, contingent on NOI targets) -- dilution of ~0.4% if fully earned, and it is only paid in the outcome where NOI outperforms. Held flat thereafter: SBC is expensed in the flows; buybacks FY2025 $0 (FY2024 $200M), so the flat count is a modelling convention, not something PSA funds every year.
inputs.debt_memo: NOT deducted (AFFO is post-interest and post-preferred-dividend; deducting would charge debt twice). For the record: notes payable $10,180.2M at 2026-06-30 (8-K ex99.1 balance sheet) + $900M senior notes issued July 2026 (4.700% 2032 / 5.150% 2036) + NSA consolidated debt assumed at close (not disclosed in documents read; NSA JV's $2.0B mortgage is non-recourse and unconsolidated at PSA's 20%); cash $259.9M. Preferred equity $4,350M liquidation preference (legacy series F-S) + NSA-legacy Series T/U shares and Series T-1 OP preferred units (~$0.4B, 6.000%) -- their dividends are below Core FFO to common, so they are already charged in the flow. Net debt/EBITDA 2.9x, (net debt + preferred)/EBITDA 4.2x at Q2-26; A2/A ratings.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the flow is post-interest and post-preferred: 10y UST ~5.24% (2026-10-01) + beta 0.75 x 5.0% ERP = 9.0%. Beta below the REIT norm (O used 0.85) because PSA carries the lowest leverage in the sector (A2/A) and month-to-month storage leases have historically shown below-REIT-average cash-flow volatility. Same rate in every scenario (risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights). +/-50bp on CoE moves base IV by roughly +/-9%.
inputs.lease_treatment: None material: PSA owns its facilities; ground-lease cost is inside self-storage cost of operations and therefore inside Core FFO. lease_cost_pct_path 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI pre-merger was ~$3M/quarter of net income (subsidiary partnerships), already excluded from 'Core FFO allocable to common shares'. Post-merger OP units (6.86M) are added to the share count rather than deducted, since the run-rate Core FFO is applied per common-equivalent unit.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (same pattern as MAA, O, GPT.AX, GMG.AX). Routing: PSA is a self-storage REIT -- the dcf-methods routing table sends REITs to AFFO capitalisation at CoE with net debt never subtracted. No prior DCF and no memory entry, so no prior model to reconcile against. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = pro forma consolidated revenue (real); 'EBITDA' line = Core FFO allocable to common + SBC (i.e. post-interest, post-preferred-dividend, pre-SBC); sbc_pct = SBC + award withholding tax; D&A = 0 and cash tax = 0 (REIT; the ~$8M/yr of TRS/foreign income tax is already inside Core FFO); capex_pct = recurring 'capital expenditures to maintain real estate facilities' (H1-26 $88.9M legacy, annualised ~$180M + ~$50M NSA/Canada = ~$230M = 4.07% of revenue) plus the remaining committed development/expansion spend of $431.6M over 18-24 months (Q2-26 release) in FY2027-28. Energy-efficiency/rebranding capex the company excludes from FAD is treated as growth investment and NOT funded inside the flows -- correspondingly the growth paths contain only organic growth (same-store rent/occupancy, lease-up of the 441-facility non-same-store pool and committed developments, NSA synergies, PS Canada NOI ramp), NOT growth from future acquisitions funded with retained cash, because the full AFFO is already counted as owner cash. FY0 PRO FORMA: FY2026 Core FFO/share guidance midpoint $16.90 ($16.75-$17.05, raised at Q2) applied to 195.0M pro forma units = $3,296M Core FFO; management says NSA is accretive within year one (so per-unit pro forma ~= standalone) and adds $0.35-$0.50/share once $110-130M of synergies are realised over 3-4 years. Pro forma revenue $5,650M = legacy FY2026 run-rate ~$4,950M (H1-26 $2,450.6M) + consolidated NSA ex the 313 JV properties ~$600M + PS Canada ~$100M (US$1.2B at a high-5s NOI yield). Margin (Core FFO + SBC)/revenue = 59.4% pro forma vs 61.4% legacy H1-26, the gap being NSA's lower (~70% vs 78%) property margins and acquisition-debt interest. Revenue is the least certain anchor; it is a scale, not a value driver -- the value is set by margin x revenue = $3,354M, which ties to guidance. FY2026 is a transition year (two acquisitions, new CEO/CFO, HQ move to Texas): the pro forma FY0 is NOT reported history, and FY2027 is the first year the reported numbers will contain the combined business for a full year. Year 1 = FY2027, discounted a full year from the valuation date (slightly conservative given the Oct-26 valuation date).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Long-run organic AFFO/unit growth judgment (base terminal growth 3.0%), not a historical CAGR. Core FFO/share FY2022 $16.31 -> FY2025 $16.97 is +1.3%/yr, the trough-cycle organic rate; the 5-year 8.7% (FY2020 $11.21) and revenue 10.6% contain the 2021-22 pandemic storage boom and ~$7B of acquisitions (ezStorage, All Storage, Simply Self Storage) and are not repeatable organically.
historical_growth.fcf_series_note: fcf_*_cagr use operating cash flow from Metrics.csv (FY2020 $2,043M, FY2022 $3,117M, FY2025 $3,186M) because XBRL capex tags stop in FY2019; Core FFO/share history from the company's earnings releases.
historical_growth.eps_note: EPS 3yr CAGR null: FY2022 EPS $23.64 contains the ~$2.1B gain on the PS Business Parks stake sale. EPS 5yr FY2020 $6.29 -> FY2025 $9.04. GAAP EPS for a REIT is depreciation- and FX-distorted; Core FFO is the earnings series.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.7% 5yr, -2.8% 3yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (10.6%) and EPS (7.5%). Expected for a REIT that distributes ~100% of taxable income and paid a $13.15/share special dividend in 2022: book equity is not a growth measure here. Revenue CAGR is acquisition-inflated; the 2026 NSA/PS Canada deals will inflate FY2027 reported revenue growth by ~15% with no per-share equivalent.
historical_growth.notes: No SBC-vs-FCF divergence to flag: SBC is ~1% of revenue and roughly flat in dollars ($41.6M FY2023, $44.7M FY2024, $39.9M FY2025).

base.margin_rationale: +2.0pp over FY2027-30 from ~$115M of the $110-130M NSA synergies (2.0% of revenue) and modest operating leverage, offset by ~0.3pp/yr of refinancing drag as 3.3%-average legacy debt rolls into the 4.7-5.15% market (2026 issues), netting to +2.0pp by FY2030 and flat after.
base.growth_rationale: Same-store revenue turns from -0.2% (FY2026 guide midpoint) to +2-3% as move-in rents (+1.6% Q2-26, first positive since 2021) flow through and new supply falls; non-same-store lease-up and committed developments add ~1pp early; PS Canada guided to high-single-digit NOI growth. Fades to 2.5% (inflation-plus-a-little) by FY2035.

scenario_narratives.base: Self-storage troughs in 2026 as management says: positive move-in rent growth and collapsing new-supply starts lift same-store revenue to +2-3% from 2027, the non-same-store pool and committed developments lease up, and NSA integration delivers most of the $110-130M synergy target over three to four years. That synergy uplift is largely consumed by refinancing 3.3%-coupon debt into a ~5% market, so Core FFO per unit grows ~4-5% a year through 2030 and then settles at an inflation-plus rate. No credit for future acquisitions beyond what retained AFFO would fund, because the full AFFO is already counted as owner cash.
scenario_narratives.bull: Supply starvation plus a housing-turnover recovery (mortgage rates easing, existing-home sales normalising) gives PSA several years of pricing power: same-store revenue +4-5%, NSA's ~70% property margins converge toward PSA's ~78% under PS Next (the top of the synergy range and then some), PS Canada's high-single-digit NOI growth materialises, and tenant reinsurance and third-party management scale on the larger base. The market re-rates to ~19x terminal AFFO on a visibly re-accelerating sector leader.
scenario_narratives.bear: Housing mobility stays depressed and Sunbelt oversupply lingers, so same-store revenue stays near flat for two more years; NSA integration under a brand-new CEO/CFO and a California-to-Texas HQ move delivers well under the synergy target while NSA's weaker portfolio needs reinvestment; legacy low-coupon debt and the new acquisition debt reprice at ~5%+, and property-tax reassessment keeps expense growth above revenue growth. Core FFO per unit is flat-to-down through 2028 and margins erode ~2pp; the market settles at ~14x AFFO, where storage REITs traded in the 2022-24 de-rating.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): two simultaneous acquisitions, a full C-suite turnover and an HQ relocation in one year is concentrated execution risk, and the refinancing drag is contractual rather than speculative. Base 55%: management's stated trough (first positive move-in rents since 2021, raised FY2026 guide) is corroborated by falling supply starts. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs a housing-turnover recovery AND above-target synergies AND no rate shock at once -- three independent things -- and A2/A balance-sheet strength protects the downside more than it enlarges the upside.

valuation_philosophy.summary: PSA is valued as the stream of AFFO (Core FFO after maintenance capex and with SBC charged as a real cost) that belongs to common and OP-unit holders, capitalised at a 9% cost of equity. Debt and preferreds are not subtracted: their cost is already inside the flow. The 2026 acquisitions are captured by re-basing FY0 to a pro forma run-rate on the enlarged 195M-unit count, not by projecting the reported revenue jump. Growth is organic only, so the valuation does not pay twice for retained cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: the 10y Treasury at ~5.24% is the single biggest lever; +/-50bp on CoE moves base IV ~+/-9%.
Pro forma FY0 is an estimate: NSA consolidated revenue and assumed debt were not in the documents read; the Q3-26 10-Q (first quarter with NSA) should be used to re-anchor revenue, margin and units.
Refinancing drag: ~$1B/yr of 3%-ish debt rolling to ~5% is a contractual headwind that offsets most of the synergy upside.
Integration under new leadership: synergy shortfall at NSA (1,000+ properties, lower margins) is the bear axis.
Same-store demand: month-to-month leases reprice quickly in either direction; housing turnover is the driver.
Excluded upside: PS Canada earn-out (only paid if NOI outperforms) and future acquisitions/developments funded by retained AFFO at spreads above the cost of equity.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 256.54-335.55
data_sources.financials: PSA_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL FY2006-Q2 2026); Q2-2026 earnings release 8-K ex99.1 (filed 2026-07-29) for Core FFO, FAD, maintenance capex, SBC, balance sheet and FY2026 guidance; 10-Q Q2-2026 cover (175,621,134 shares at 2026-07-21); NSA merger close 8-K (2026-07-22: 0.1400 exchange ratio, 4.10M OP units, Series T/U/T-1 preferred); NSA 10-Q Q1-2026 cover (77,212,533 NSA common at 2026-05-01); PS Canada close release 8-K ex99.1 (2026-09-01: 2.76M OP units at $321.98, $310M cash, earn-out up to $288M at $375/unit).
